items.description: One world-scoped rule: a condition over world facts and the effects that follow — the same primitive a kit's per-body actions already run on (ActionPredicate, ActionEffect, ActionTriggerMode), widened to the world's own scope rather than a sibling engine with its own vocabulary. There is no scheduler and no trigger taxonomy beside this: time is just another fact.

name.description: The rule's stable name — unique within the section, the WorldMutation.UpsertWorldRule/WorldMutation.RemoveWorldRule key, and the world.rules read-back line. A WorldCellName, the same validated-identifier type a state row and a cell key ride: dot-free and free of the reserved character set, refused by name (naming the offending character) at the JSON converter before a document can hold one. The reserved $ prefix is refused on top of that, by CompileAll — exactly as it is for a state row name, and for the same reason: $ marks what the engine mints, and nothing mints a rule.

effects.description: The effects applied in order when the rule fires. With a Decision, these are common entry effects and may be empty.

gate.description: The predicate that must hold, or null for always.

mode.description: Without a Decision, whether the rule fires every tick the gate holds (Level, the default) or once per crossing (Edge). A rule that writes a row almost always wants Edge: level-firing an addState is what wrote 503 journal entries in 500 ticks.

forEach.description: A keyed state row to iterate, or null for one evaluation per tick. With a row named, the gate and effects evaluate once per cell the row holds at the top of the tick, with $each bound to that cell's key — the quantifier that lets one rule tick a status for every body carrying it, or one rule judge every piece or card of a keyed row. An integer key also binds the each body reference; a non-integer key binds $each alone. The latch is kept per key, by the key's value when it is an integer and by its position in the row otherwise.

decision.description: Optional choice policy; requires Level mode. Common effects run only when entering a selected option.

options.description: One to 32 uniquely named options, in deterministic tie-break order.

items.description: One candidate in a decision; its score is read only when its gate holds.

score.description: A numeric expression in the decision's score kind. Arithmetic failure makes this option ineligible for that reconsideration.

effects.description: Effects fired when entering this option; may be empty for an inspection-only choice.

gate.description: Eligibility predicate, or null for always eligible.

neighbors.description: Optional bounded nearby-body expansion. Requires rule forEach; each and left identify the observer, right the candidate, only inside this option's gate, score, and effects. A different individual is a selection transition.

range.description: Inclusive spherical radius, in world units, from one Q48.16 unit through 1,000,000.

candidateBudget.description: Maximum inspected points per reconsideration, including self, rejected points, and an incumbent recheck.

maxCandidates.description: Maximum candidates scored, from 1 through 32 and no greater than CandidateBudget.

halfAngleDegrees.description: Forward cone half-angle in (0,180]; coincident points are perceptible.

requiresLineOfSight.description: Whether candidates must pass the world's solid-field sight query.

retainCurrent.description: Spend one inspection on the current individual first. If still perceptible and eligible, reserve one retained slot for it. A budget of one can spend all attention on the incumbent.

periodSeconds.description: Positive exact engine-tick duration between reconsiderations. First evaluation is immediate.

scoreKind.description: The common numeric kind, Int or Fixed; operands must match it.

commitmentSeconds.description: Non-negative exact duration protecting a newly selected option from ordinary reconsideration.

incumbentBonus.description: Non-negative score bonus for retaining the current eligible option and individual. In weighted mode it cannot revive a non-positive weight.

seed.description: Authored seed combined with the world seed, rule name, binding key, and body generation.

interrupt.description: An optional rising-edge predicate that bypasses period and commitment. Losing eligibility also bypasses both.

onNoChoice.description: Effects fired when an enabled decision first finds no choice, loses its choice, or its enclosing gate closes while a choice is held.
